newsitem.title: USA: Bethlehem Steel to upgrade Indiana plant.
newsitem.headline: Bethlehem Steel to upgrade Indiana plant.

text.p: Bethlehem Steel Corp said its board has approved $70 million of spending to modernize the No.1 continuous slab caster at its Burn Harbor Division in Indiana.

To minimize the impact on Burns Harbor's operations, modernization of the caster will take place during the same time period in 1998 that the Division's "D" blast furnace is scheduled for reline, the company said.
Customer deliveries and service will be maintained by building inventories of slabs prior to the equipment outages, Bethlehem Steel said.
Bethlehem Steel said extensive technical modifications will be made to the caster to improve slab quality, increase productivity and reduce production costs.
Burns Harbor accounts for about half of Bethlehem's total revenues and the mills costs are fully competitive with mini-mills entering the marketplace, the company said.
Bethlehem Steel reported 1996 revenues of $4.7 billion.
Burns Harbor's No. 1 caster accounts for about one-third of the Division's cast slab production, Bethlehem Steel said.

Improvements to the No. 1 slab caster -- together with a recent series of modernizations at Burns Harbor's hot strip mill and 160-inch plate mill -- is consistent with Bethlehem's strategy of keeping the mill competitive, Bethlehem said.
